- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price by 2–5% in early forecast window; adjust downward by 1–2% for first 7–10 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 2–4 days; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
